text:
Michael Misa, the second overall pick in 2025, is 19 and playing like a teenager the Sharks trust. His ice time is up 2.7 minutes over his last ten games compared with his season, and he has 14 points in 27 games, right on a league-average scoring rate. The shooting is honest: 5 goals on 5.6 expected, 12.5% against a 13.5% league norm. Nothing about his production is running on luck.

The harder part is the even-strength game. San Jose gets 40.6% of the expected goals at 5v5 with him on the ice, more than five points worse than without him. That's the cost of a young centre learning against top lines on a rebuilding team, and it's the number we'd watch over the winter.

The recent signs are good. He carried a four-game point streak into last week, including a shorthanded goal on the rush against Seattle on Nov. 21. History is on his side too: of 47 forwards picked in the top four since 2005 with four-plus seasons, all 47 reached 200 NHL games.
headline: Misa's second season is about minutes, not points
